scope: R140 eight-window A53-only compiler comparison; no deployment

rules.pairing: Same window and lane; eight non-reused A53/R136 pairs, plus independent same-window A53/C comparisons.
rules.primary: In each window take the equal-weight geometric mean of seven latency-mean A53/R136 ratios. Median across eight windows < 0.98 and at least seven window geometric means < 1.
rules.latency_veto: Any individual lane mean/p95/p99 A53/R136 ratio median > 1.03 and at least seven of eight ratios > 1 rejects the candidate.
rules.secondary: Report register_1 p95 against both controls separately; it cannot override the primary or latency veto.
rules.resources: Report all process-clock CPU, ELF bytes, and daemon before/after VmRSS/RssAnon/VmData/VmHWM snapshots and increases. No full-memory equivalence claim.
rules.numeric: Lane ratios use exact fractions. Window geometric means use 60-digit Decimal arithmetic rounded to 30 decimal places before median and strict gate comparisons.
rules.interpretation: Equal weights are an engineering selection, not a traffic mix, a 9:1 business score, significance, equivalence, or whole-system dominance.
rules.stopping: Exactly eight complete clean windows and all 168 cases; no retries, exclusions, changed thresholds, or data-dependent extra windows.

limitations: Equal weights are an engineering choice, not real traffic or a 9:1 business score. Frozen engineering gates are not statistical significance or equivalence.
All eight windows and 168 cases are retained. Historical R136/R139 and Oracle timing observations are excluded.
CPU is fully reported without a statistical CPU veto; substantial unexpected costs still need engineering assessment. A passed rule is not deployment authorization.
Original caller has no live CPU placement/context snapshots. Parent allowance and exact launch argv are verified; there is no per-operation migration or scheduling trace.
Daemon CPU is recomputed from process-clock snapshots; caller CPU has a delta only. Provider CPU is excluded. No wall-minus-CPU inference is made.
Resident values describe before/after the seven-lane lifecycle; VmHWM is a process high-water value. PSS, full peak attribution, long-term retention and full R136 memory fixtures are not revalidated.
One-object lookup/invoke sentinels and registration-generated events do not cover general user SEND, all other lanes, or nine-component integration.
Guard assertions cover config/mount/production identity inside each window; exact inputs and same health/boot agree across windows. Raw host process identities are not separately archived.
